beats.text: You think you can tell when someone is lying. You can't.
A huge review pooled over two hundred studies, with almost twenty-five thousand people judging lies and truths.
Their accuracy: fifty-four percent. A coin flip gets fifty.
Actual lies were caught less than half the time. Forty-seven percent.
We mostly assume people tell the truth. So most lies slip right through.
Your gut feeling? Basically a coin flip, with confidence.

sources: Bond & DePaulo (2006). Accuracy of deception judgments. Personality and Social Psychology Review 10(3). Meta-analysis: 206 documents, 24,483 judges; 54% correct; 47% of lies and 61% of truths correctly classified. Via SAGE abstract.
